geographyClimate.claim: Urban heat island — EPA framing (use this exact framing)
geographyClimate.value: Per the U.S. EPA: in the United States the heat island effect makes daytime air temperatures in urban areas about 1–7°F higher than outlying areas, and nighttime temperatures about 2–5°F higher; HUMID regions (primarily the eastern U.S.) and LARGER, DENSER cities experience the greatest differences — a framing that fits Newark (dense, eastern-U.S. city). Use the EPA national range; do NOT assert a Newark-specific number.
geographyClimate.source: U.S. EPA, 'What Are Heat Islands?' / 'Learn About Heat Islands' (epa.gov/heatislands)

geographyClimate.claim: Urban heat island — roof/surface temperature framing
geographyClimate.value: Per the U.S. EPA, urban surfaces (buildings, roads, roofs) absorb and re-emit the sun's heat far more than natural landscapes; conventional roofs reach much higher SURFACE temperatures than air temperature. EPA: green roofs can have surface temperatures up to 56°F lower than conventional roofs and can reduce nearby air temperatures by up to 20°F. (Conventional dark roofs commonly run far above air temperature in summer — keep this qualitative unless quoting EPA's green-roof differential.)
geographyClimate.source: U.S. EPA, 'Using Green Roofs to Reduce Heat Islands' and 'Reduce Heat Islands' (epa.gov/heatislands)

geographyClimate.value: Newark is essentially a basin sloping toward the Passaic River; elevation rises from 0 ft (sea level) in the east (Ironbound/meadowlands) to ~230 ft above sea level in the western section (Forest Hill, Vailsburg, toward the Watchung ridge area). cautions: CORRECTION: Do NOT attribute Newark construction permits to the 'Department of Economic & Housing Development, Division of Buildings' (the baseline pack's assumption). The City of Newark's own .gov site assigns construction permitting and UCC enforcement to the OFFICE OF UNIFORM CONSTRUCTION CODE / BUILDING DIVISION within the DEPARTMENT OF ENGINEERING (City Hall, Room B23). Economic & Housing Development is a development/policy department, not the UCC enforcing agency. Use 'Newark Department of Engineering — Building Division / Office of Uniform Construction Code.'

Do NOT say a detached one- or two-family reroof in Newark needs a permit. Per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 it is 'ordinary maintenance' — no permit, no inspection, no notice. The permit/25% rule is for commercial, multi-family, and attached buildings only.

Do NOT assert that any specific Newark home needs a Certificate of Appropriateness without confirming (a) the parcel is in a LOCALLY designated district or is a locally designated landmark under Newark Municipal Code Chapter 41:10, and (b) it is a contributing property. Newark's hook is real (Chapter 41:10 auto-designates pre-May-30-2007 Register sites as local), but Register-boundary ≠ contributing-status for an individual parcel, and post-2007 Register listings are NOT automatically local.

Forest Hill: do NOT describe it as 'National-Register-only / no local restriction.' Forest Hill Historic District is on the National Register (1990) AND, because it predates May 30, 2007, is auto-designated a LOCAL Newark historic district under Chapter 41:10 — so a COA does apply to exterior roofing work on contributing properties there.

Quote the ordinance accurately: Chapter 41:10 auto-designates pre-2007 Register sites as a 'local historic site or district' (not necessarily the word 'landmark'). Frame the COA gate around 'locally designated historic site/district or landmark,' and cite 'Newark Municipal Code Chapter 41:10' rather than inventing a sub-section number.

Urban heat island: do NOT publish a Newark-specific number like '10–15°F hotter than the suburbs' or 'roof surface temps reduced 50°F' as fact. Use the EPA national framing: daytime ~1–7°F and nighttime ~2–5°F higher in urban areas, greatest in humid eastern-U.S. and dense cities (which fits Newark). For roof/surface heat, use EPA's green-roof figures (surface up to 56°F lower; air up to 20°F lower) or keep qualitative.

Do NOT state an exact Newark 'total housing units (2020 Census)' or 'percent built before 1940' as a precise Census figure unless verified directly on Census QuickFacts / ACS B25034. The available figures (~118,991 units ACS; ~23.7–25% pre-1940; median year built ~1966) are secondary aggregators — frame qualitatively ('roughly 115,000–120,000 housing units'; 'about a quarter of Newark's homes predate 1940').

Geography precision: the Passaic River is Newark's EASTERN/northeastern boundary and drains to NEWARK BAY (south/southeast); the Hackensack River and meadowlands are WEST of Newark Bay, not within Newark. Don't conflate the Passaic and Hackensack. EWR is partly in Newark AND partly in Elizabeth (Essex/Union line) — don't call it 'entirely in Newark.'

historic.claim: COA process — binding for designated districts/sites; roofing is in scope
historic.value: A Certificate of Appropriateness from the Orange HPC is required to deviate from the Design Guidelines in the alteration/rehabilitation/construction of any property in an APPROVED Historic District or a property designated historically significant by City Council or in the Master Plan historic preservation element. For property in a designated district the COA is DECISIONAL/BINDING (the Commission must decide the COA, not merely advise); the HPC plays an advisory role to the Planning/Zoning Board for development applications. Roofing-related exterior work is within COA scope (HPC resolutions cover roof solar panels and new construction). Emergency repairs to protect health/safety/habitability may proceed without first obtaining a COA. A COA is separate from and does not replace a UCC construction permit.

X, COA definition + §210-93 (ecode360.com/34568641); City of Orange Township HPC resolutions (616 Lincoln Ave — Montrose-Seven Oaks district; 338 Elizabeth St — roof solar; orangetwpnjcc.org); HPC public meeting June 19, 2024 ('it's in a designated district... this commission has to decide the certificate of appropriateness... that takes it out of the advisory')

cautions: DO NOT assert that any Irvington home or neighborhood requires a Certificate of Appropriateness (COA). Irvington has no local Historic Preservation Commission and no locally designated historic district found in research. Per the NPS, listing alone places no restriction — and here there are no NRHP listings in Irvington anyway. Corrected framing: 'Irvington has no local historic-district ordinance, so a homeowner reroof faces no Certificate-of-Appropriateness step' (verify against the current municipal code before publishing as absolute).

DO NOT publish a specific 'percent of housing built before 1940/1950,' a renter-occupancy %, or a 5+-unit %. The exact ACS figures (e.g. the ~18% pre-1940 / ~70% renter numbers seen in one secondary aggregator pass) could NOT be verified against data.census.gov or a named ACS table. Corrected framing: describe the stock qualitatively as 'older, predominantly early-20th-century housing' and 'a dense, rental- and multi-family-heavy market.' Only publish a number if pulled directly from a named ACS table (B25034/B25003/B25024 or DP04) for Irvington.

DO NOT call 'Hilton' an Irvington neighborhood. Hilton is a section of MAPLEWOOD on the Maplewood side of the Springfield Avenue / Irvington border (confirmed via Springfield Avenue Partnership and NeighborhoodScout). Corrected framing: 'the Hilton section of neighboring Maplewood, just across Irvington's western Springfield Avenue border.'

DO NOT call 'Vailsburg' an Irvington neighborhood. Vailsburg is a NEWARK neighborhood adjacent to Irvington's eastern edge. Corrected framing: 'near Newark's Vailsburg section, across Irvington's eastern border.'

DO NOT present Olympic Park as a current amusement park or attraction. It operated 1887-1965 and closed; it survives only as the origin of the 'Olympic Park' neighborhood NAME (its entrance was on Chancellor Avenue; the park straddled the Irvington/Maplewood line). Frame strictly as history.

DO NOT assert Irvington-specific microclimate numbers (UHI degrees, local wind/temperature/snow figures). Only the shared EWR/NOAA baseline is sourced. Any heat-island statement must be qualitative ('dense, built-out township with limited tree canopy retains summer heat'), not a numeric UHI delta.

DO NOT say I-78 runs THROUGH the middle of Irvington. The sourced fact is that I-78 passes 'very briefly along the southeastern border at Exit 54' (Wikipedia). Frame it as bordering/touching the southeastern edge.

DO NOT pin a single official department name with certainty. Sources show both 'Construction Code Department' (Chapter 240 ordinance) and 'Building Construction'/'Housing and Building' (township website), and gave conflicting director names (Tharien Karim-Arnold, Director of Building and Housing, vs. Joseph Ouseley). Use the generic safe phrasing 'the Township of Irvington's construction-code (building) office' and do not name a specific director or fee on-page without live verification.

DO NOT state that a permit is required for a normal Irvington home reroof. Under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 a detached 1-2 family reroof is ordinary maintenance statewide — Irvington's local enforcement does not change that. (Commercial / multi-family / attached buildings exceeding the 25% rule do require a permit, consistent with Irvington's high multi-family share.)
